summary: Added the missing datetime import that crashed every admin page rendering a timestamp, and argued for keeping the except clause narrow rather than widening it to swallow the next NameError; 19 passed and the sabotage reproduced the user's exact error.
Drafted the upstream issue about the Bash/PowerShell guard inconsistency into the working tree per the human's decision; verified present, all four elements found, and confirmed NOT posted.

Superseded: the brain path is already in the gitignored .env's ALLOWED_DOCS_DIRS, which server.py loads at import, so issue #17's first request is satisfied by configuration on this machine; the remaining gap is that no live test pins the allowlist.

Pinned the directory allowlist with six collected tests covering the four data_dir defaults, the env-var extension, the cwd exclusion and its opt-in, plus a permanent negative control that mutates allowed_dirs in memory; they pass unchanged under a hostile ambient ALLOWED_DOCS_DIRS, and kb/core.py is byte-identical to its pre-dispatch hash.

check_updates now sends a per-document progress notification with no fabricated total (using the item field only per-document events carry), the up-front event keeps its real total_docs, and my sabotage of the total fix failed the new assertion before restore.

Added a per-document progress callback to check_all_updates and a cost warning to the tool schema - and established, by reading the server and the mcp package, that no MCP client can see mid-call progress from this server at all, so the honest deliverable is an operator-visible log heartbeat plus a warning before the call; 4 passed.

Added the missing allowlist guard to check_url_updates before its unbounded network path, with 2 new tests - but the agent proved, and I confirmed, that this is NOT the tool issue #17 names, so the issue stays open and a re-scoping task was opened.

Closed by measurement rather than by a fix: a concurrent Thread.start() blocks at most ~155 ms during the embeddings warm-up - one 263 MB torch DLL, not the 3.5 s import - which I reproduced independently at 154 and 161 ms, so the task's own 'a second or two' threshold says leave it alone, and the title's 'for the import duration' premise is retracted.

Bounded the embeddings load behind a deadline on a named warm-up thread after re-measuring that faiss, numpy AND sentence_transformers all stall under a pending stdin read; 58 passed, and the agent caught its own broken harness when the known-positive control failed to stall.

Moved the no-LLM refusal to queue time so no job row or queue entry is ever created - the right design, 26 passed in its own file with the sabotage reproducing the old per-job pattern - but the full suite shows two tests in files outside its grant that queue extraction without an LLM and now get refused; partial until those stub an LLM client.

Root-caused the long-lived-stdio search hang to Windows serialising I/O on the stdin file object - a BLAS-linked import inside nltk blocks until a client message completes the transport's pending read - refuting both candidates the plan named, and bounded it with a deadline; 34 passed and I reproduced the mechanism independently.

SUPERSEDES the earlier record: the cause is not process death but a heavyweight lazy nltk/scipy import inside the unlogged window in search(), proven by a stack dump of a live blocked process and by a cancellation that produced no completion line.

A real stdio client now observes the ack plus repeated heartbeat ticks from one add_document call stalled on a test-held SQLite lock released after 1s (5.8s test, 15s bound, was 30.8s vs 30s), my server-side sabotage of the repeat fails it with "got 2", and the full suite is 441 passed / 4 skipped.

Re-scoped issue #17's second request out of existence with the measurement rather than a reading: check_updates takes one boolean and no path, so it cannot fail fast on a disallowed one, and the 1800s stall was a 323-document re-index running correctly with no progress output - the read-only scan takes 2.66s over 1,138 documents.

Replaced the parked stdin read with a PeekNamedPipe-polling reader on Windows so the nltk import no longer serialises behind client messages; the liveness sweep went from 4 timeouts in 103s to zero in 34s, the first search from 5.02s degraded to 0.63s with the real stemmer, and my own sabotage of the platform switch fails the new case in 48s naming both tools.

Put the pid in the shared log format with a test that checks the formatted output rather than the source string - and, chasing the one failure the agent wrote off as an unrelated flake, found it was deterministic and its own: MCPSession never drained the server's stderr, and startup logging sits 185 bytes under a 4096-byte pipe buffer. Drain moved into the session; 40 passed.

Replaced Mount('/mcp') with two explicit Routes over an ASGI class instance so the bare path serves 200 instead of 307-redirecting; 31 passed and restoring the Mount reproduced the exact reported redirect.

Wired real notifications/progress through call_tool - an immediate ack before dispatch, a 15s heartbeat, and an emit_tool_progress() a handler can adopt from a worker thread via a contextvar - proved by a client reading frames off the wire rather than by a method-call assertion, and it refuted both the dispatch's SDK version and the prior task's claim that the SDK offered nothing.
Passed version=__version__ into the Server(...) construction so clients are told the project's version instead of the MCP SDK's; 32 passed and dropping the argument again made the new case fail.

Root-caused the cascade to an undrained stderr pipe in the test harness itself - not a product defect - fixed it, and the suite now passes skip-by-default with the assertion intact; the full repo is green at 412 passed / 4 skipped for the first time, and a real scrape_url hang was found and left in scope for whoever can touch util.py.

Replaced the sleeping stand-in with one that holds the lock the search path actually takes, and added the missing case pairing tool calls with the live extraction worker; 41 passed, and my own re-run of the sabotage confirms the new blocker fails the assertion in 1.66s where the old one never could.

Replaced the raw PRAGMA data_version gate with a corpus fingerprint over documents and chunks, so a peer's telemetry write no longer drops the chunk cache, the BM25 index and every search cache; 13 passed, both sabotages discriminated, and an existing test caught a real ABA hole in the first design.

Root-caused the scrape hang to two defects no hypothesis in the plan named - mdscrape inheriting the MCP client's stdin pipe, and a refused connect being retried with backoff - taking scrape_url from never returning to 4.8s; partial because the liveness suite stays red for a separate loader-lock defect outside its grant, and because it refuted two claims the brief asserted, both of them mine.

Chose quieten-startup with a budget: stderr now carries WARNING and above by default while server.log keeps INFO, taking startup stderr from 3911 bytes to ~65 against a 4096-byte buffer; a 1024-byte budget test and a knob test that proves it is not vacuous both pass, and the sabotage fails the budget at 4509 bytes.

All 32 TDZ_ variables the code reads are now documented with code-read defaults (the real gap was 16, not 13), CLAUDE.md's stale line count and missing polling-stdin note are fixed, and I re-derived the zero-gap grep and sampled five defaults against the code.
TO-DOS.md's two fixed admin-GUI entries are struck through with DONE markers citing 89e7710 and 609f764, confirmed against module-scope imports in the code, and no other section was touched.

Bounded tool dispatch with an opt-out default plus a separate lock-wait bound, after measuring that the 'one hang kills the server' half is HTTP-only and stdio was already concurrent; 37 passed and the sabotage failed on a deadline rather than hanging.

Stubbed an LLM into the two tests the queue-time guard had broken - env vars in-process for the figure-OCR one and on the subprocess env for the startup one, since its KB runs in a child interpreter - leaving the guard and the overlap assertion untouched; the full suite is 429 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed on my own re-run, green for the first time in this drain.

Hoisted both function-local imports to module scope, killing the page-load crash and the Run-Check crash together, and replaced the vacuous page-render coverage with a case that injects a document carrying source_url and scrape_config; 20 passed and the sabotage reproduced the user's exact error.
